caveats: T1/T2 have identical variable cost (2.456978 $/GJ), so their split is degenerate; combined T1+T2 is the stable quantity.
The RNWBIO cost is a scenario input; it is not a fitted biomass price.
Case B caps are diagnostic scenarios, not policy recommendations.
All other assumptions are inherited from the committed stress run.

activation_thresholds.interpretation: T3/T4 require rest-of-Canada BCW demand above the T1+T2 capacity. RNWBIO is the sole BIO producer and does not substitute for BCW in end uses; raising its cost cannot raise BCW demand. A binding cap is infeasible.
